safar. / DESIGN NOTES
DESTINATIONS FIRST. PAYMENTS STAY SEPARATE.

One clear decision
at a time.

Select all requested destinations first. Walk through passenger counts in that order. Then collect a separate payment for each destination and hand over printed tickets.

RUSH / QUICK ENTRY

Keep the next passenger moving.

Fixed destination buttons, a visible default of one passenger, direct count controls and a fresh unpaid repeat journey. Rush and Guided share the same queue. Pending UPI does not block another ticket. Cash received & print is an explicit confirmation, never triggered by selecting a stop.

CORRECT / BEFORE PAYMENT

A clear way back.

Edit an unpaid ticket’s destination and count, then save. Back discards corrections. Paid or pending tickets stay locked. Each request number follows its payment and printed slip. Cash shortcuts calculate change without confirming receipt automatically.

01 / SELECT

One stop or several.

Single destination replaces the selected stop. Multiple destinations uses visible checkmarks and numbered selection order. The full route supports uncommon stops. Nothing requires typing on the common path.

02 / COUNT

Every destination gets its turn.

A single destination card asks for its own passenger count. One-tap choices cover common counts; More supports 1–99 adults. Next advances through every selected destination. A progress strip makes completed counts and the next stop visible.

03 / COLLECT

Independent payments.

Each destination has its own amount, Cash/UPI choice, status and reference. There is no combined bill or shared payment QR. A UPI request is tied to that destination and exact amount. Pending requests must be resolved before switching to cash, preventing accidental double collection.

04 / PRINT

Only paper tickets.

Payment and delivery are separate: online payment still produces a paper ticket. Print all paid journeys together, or an individual paid ticket while another payment is pending. Each destination produces a distinct group ticket. No digital-ticket delivery is offered.

05 / RECOVER

Retry a slip, never a charge.

Ticket records are saved before printing. Repeated print actions reuse those IDs. If paper runs out, retry only unprinted slips. Successful payments and pending requests survive a refresh in browser storage. Paid journey details are locked; production corrections need an explicit operator cancellation/refund process.

06 / REACH

Thumb controls, readable context.

Large destination tiles, direct quantity buttons and a fixed bottom action. Boarding context remains visible. Selection, payment and print states use words and shapes as well as colour. The reach overlay is illustrative and must be validated on the intended phone, with both hands and controlled motion.

Assumptions and prototype limits

  • Route, stop order and fares are illustrative. All selected destinations share a boarding stop captured before the flow.
  • Passengers for one destination travel as one adult-fare group and share one ticket and payment. Unrelated payers travelling to the same stop use separate queue entries in Rush, with separate payment references and slips.
  • Cash received is confirmed by the conductor. UPI is a simulation: there is no real merchant, money transfer or payment provider. The sample QR is explicitly non-payable.
  • Real UPI confirmation must come from the payment service, not a passenger screenshot or a conductor success button. Every destination needs its own transaction reference and verified amount.
  • Online payment needs connectivity. Cash ticketing can be demonstrated offline with queued synchronization; production requires operator-approved offline issuance.
  • Printing uses a hypothetical wearable thermal printer. Browser print layouts are available, but physical printer integration, weight, paper handling and battery life are untested.
  • One record per group, idempotent issuance, payment status checks and access controls require a durable production backend. This prototype saves data only in this browser.
THE SPEED TRADE-OFF

Clarity adds steps.

This requested guided flow is easier to follow but adds destination confirmation, sequential counts and payment actions. It is not a three-tap flow, and no under-four-second claim is made. The assignment's original speed target still needs testing and can be compared with the Rush shortcut. No measured speed improvement is claimed.

VALIDATION PLAN

Measure correct handovers.

Test different counts, uncommon stops, mixed Cash/UPI, pending payments, printer failures and interruption. Measure total queue time, per-ticket time, incorrect charges, wrong handovers and grip changes. No conductor study or real payment/printing throughput has been claimed.

Printed tickets. Separate payments. A predictable sequence.
